transcript:
Header: Redwood Inference All-Hands
Date/Time: 2026-10-11 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~75 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (CEO), Maya Chen (VP Product), Devon Park (CTO), leadership, engineering, product, sales, marketing, all staff

[00:00] Jordan Lee (CEO): Hey everyone, um, good morning, thanks for joining. Quick housekeeping — we'll record this, transcript will be posted and then we'll dive into the quarter. Sorry for the slightly delayed start.
[00:18] Jordan Lee (CEO): First up, quick win callouts — Q3 revenue was up 32% quarter over quarter, usage growth across hosted APIs and Dedicated signups beating plan. Big shout out to sales and infra teams, amazing work.
[00:35] Asha Patel (Head of Sales): Yeah, team has been grinding, pilots closed with three mid-market customers this week. A note — we're seeing more interest in private deployment for regulated verticals.
[00:50] Maya Chen (VP Product): On product, we shipped the Optimize cost recommendations beta to a subset of customers, and initial numbers show a 17% token cost reduction on average. There are some edge cases where latency bumped, we're tracking those.
[01:12] Devon Park (CTO): On reliability, we had an incident Friday — root cause was a KV cache eviction bug in the runtime when burst load crossed a threshold. Luis and crew already have a patch; full rollback and mitigation steps are in the postmortem draft.
[01:35] Luis Ortega (Head of Infra): Yep the hotfix is staged, rolling canary now. We expect full rollout by tomorrow. Also we identified a kernel selection pathway that under-allocates GPU memory for longer sequence shapes — working with the compiler folks to harden selection heuristics.
[01:58] Jordan Lee (CEO): Thanks. Real quick on product strategy — our thesis still stands: serving and economics win. We're doubling down on predictable performance across hosted, dedicated, and private. The unified API is a big differentiator.
[02:18] Maya Chen (VP Product): A quick demo highlight — Dedicated latency profiles now support per-tenant SLOs and cost tiering. Note: some of the telemetry names in the UI got scrambled in the first canary, that's being fixed (there was a label that read 'dedicate' instead of 'dedicated', so small polish).
[02:42] Emily Dawson (PM): We're also updating SDKs this week to expose the new routing policy flags and to better surfacing of per-token cost. SDK release notes will be published.
[03:05] Jordan Lee (CEO): On Private deployments — we closed two contracts for VPC private control plane, one with a finance customer in EU and another with a healthcare pilot in APAC. That pushes our on-prem and private momentum forward.
[03:30] Devon Park (CTO): Technical note: private installs required extra work on KMS integration and audit logging. We built an HSM abstraction but some bits are still manual for on-prem installers; we need to productize that.
[03:50] Maya Chen (VP Product): Also, function/tool calling and structured output ingestion questions keep coming up — we're prioritizing better examples and reference apps, and a how-to repo for embedding-based retrieval patterns.
[04:10] Jordan Lee (CEO): Hiring update — Priya?
[04:12] Priya Nambiar (Head of People): We're green-lit to hire 12 engineers this quarter: 6 infra/runtime, 3 product, 2 sales engineers, 1 security engineer. Main focus is runtime/infra to reduce time-to-serve and finish Dedicated feature set. Interviews open next week.
[04:35] Jordan Lee (CEO): OKRs — we'll circulate the final OKRs after this. High level: 1) Improve P99 latency 15% on Dedicated, 2) Reduce per-token cost via Optimize recommendations by 10% across top 20 customers, 3) Ship Private GA for VPC installs.
[05:00] Asha Patel (Head of Sales): On commercial — renewals are healthy; we have three expansion opportunities where customers want reserved pools and stricter data residency. Pricing team to work with me on bundles.
[05:20] Someone (Engineer): Quick question — did we decide on default quantization profiles for small models? There's customer confusion between 4-bit and 8-bit defaults.
[05:29] Devon Park (CTO): We landed on model-specific recommendations: for most customers 4-bit with per-model vetting; we'll automate suggestions in Optimize. We'll publish a migration guide.
[05:45] Jordan Lee (CEO): Marketing quick note — Emily and team?
[05:48] Emily Dawson (PM): We're preparing a Q4 performance brief and a public benchmark blog post. We want to be careful about model names and claims — legal is reviewing content for compliance. Also we'll do a demo day for partners.
[06:10] Jordan Lee (CEO): Alright let's open for questions from employees. Please keep them short.
[06:20] Employee 1: Were there any learnings from the outage Friday around alerting?
[06:24] Luis Ortega (Head of Infra): Yes — our thresholds were too loose for cache pressure metrics. We're adding synthetic load tests and tighter alerts; also improved dashboarding for the runtime team.
[06:40] Employee 2: Any guidance for customer-facing folks on the Dedicated SLA timeline?
[06:44] Asha Patel (Head of Sales): We should tell customers we're on track for SLA rollout in November, pending final performance validation and legal sign-off.
[06:58] Employee 3: Curious about private GA — what's blocking GA?
[07:02] Maya Chen (VP Product): Main blockers are the installer UX and automated KMS/HSM workflows. Also need some more onboarding docs and a self-test harness.
[07:22] Jordan Lee (CEO): Closing remarks — appreciate the focus. Quick recap of action items: publish the Dedicated brief, post incident retrospective, roll the hotfix, hire for infra, and ship SDK updates. Expect follow-up notes in Slack and the all-hands doc.
[07:45] Jordan Lee (CEO): Thanks everyone. End of all-hands.

Notes: transcript has some auto-caption artifacts — product names sometimes truncated, eg 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', and a few labels in the recording were misattributed. Links referenced during meeting: internal/docs/dedicated-perf-brief, internal/postmortems/2026-10-09-kv-cache, github/optimize-release-notes.
